# A Go file that does not parse leaves the loader with a recovered, partial
# AST. The template checks still run against it, and they are still worth
# running -- but what they saw was incomplete, so they say so.
#
# muxt does not fail here. go build is what gates on a package compiling;
# muxt check is additional validation layered on top, and refusing to run it
# would take away a signal rather than add one. What was wrong before is that
# the output was identical either way: a package go build rejects looked
# exactly as clean as one that passes.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
exec go build ./...

# Break a file the templates never mention.
cp broken.txt broken.go
! exec go build ./...

muxt check
stderr 'warning: package has syntax errors, so these checks ran against a partial AST; run go build for the full picture'
stdout 'ok: 1 template'

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
stderr 'warning: package has syntax errors'

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /greet Greet(ctx)" -}}
	{{- .Result -}}
{{- end -}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type T struct{}

func (T) Greet(ctx context.Context) string { return "hello" }
